clue.text: Dog in cable host's opening show

parts.note: a cable is a wire

indicators.note: the opening of the word host's is its first letter

parts.note: to show is to air, as in airing your views

explanation.surface: A dog appears at the start of a cable network's programme.
explanation.definitionFit: A wirehair is a rough-coated breed or type of terrier, so it is a kind of dog.

clue.text: Fast, but not when in France!

definitions.text: Fast, but not when in France!

parts.words: Fast, but not when in France!
parts.note: the English word for the Christian fasting season is also the French adjective meaning slow, the opposite of fast

explanation.surface: A quip that a fast stops being one once you cross the Channel.
explanation.walkthrough: In English the season before Easter is a time of fasting; in French the same spelling means 'slow', so it is 'not fast' in France.
explanation.definitionFit: The forty days before Easter are traditionally kept as a fast, and the French adjective for slow shares the spelling.

clue.text: Greek island with quiet ambiance — not half!

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

indicators.note: not half means only the front half of the word for ambiance is kept, the rest dropped

parts.note: ambiance is atmosphere

explanation.surface: A Greek island praised for its peaceful atmosphere, with the slangy exclamation 'not half!' meaning 'and how!'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half!' reads as British slang for emphatic agreement, but it tells you to keep only half of the synonym for ambiance.
explanation.definitionFit: Patmos is an island in the Aegean, part of Greece, where St John is said to have written Revelation.

clue.text: Time to invest in kites — they're seen in the sky

indicators.note: to invest in something is to put into it, so the time letter is placed inside the word for kites

parts.note: kite is old slang, chiefly RAF, for an aeroplane

explanation.surface: A suggestion to spend time flying kites, which are visible overhead.
explanation.definitionFit: Venus, Mars and Jupiter are often visible from Earth as bright points in the night sky.

clue.text: Funny hue by red borders of reseda plant genus

indicators.note: funny suggests something odd or out of order, so the three letters of hue are rearranged

parts.note: Che Guevara, the revolutionary, is a classic red

indicators.note: the borders of reseda are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A gardener describing a plant with an odd colour growing beside a reseda border.
explanation.walkthrough: Reseda is itself a plant (mignonette), which makes it look like part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Heuchera, coral bells, is a genus of perennial flowering plants in the saxifrage family.

clue.text: Make invalid's absorbing phrase open to debate

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so the word for phrase goes inside the word for make invalid

parts.note: to make invalid is to disable; the 's stands for is, linking to what follows
to phrase something is to put it, as in 'put it another way'

explanation.surface: A claim that an invalid's wording is questionable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invalid' looks like a sick person, but 'make invalid' is a verb: to disable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disputable can be argued about, so it is questionable or open to debate.

clue.text: Keep writing about new standard

indicators.note: about means around, so the words for keep writing go round the new letter

parts.note: to keep writing is to pen on, carrying on penning

explanation.surface: An exhortation to carry on writing about a new standard of conduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Standard' reads as a benchmark, but it is a flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A pennon is a long narrow flag on a lance, and a standard is also a flag or banner.

clue.text: Let go of everything, including WPC's protection

indicators.note: including means taking in, so the letter W sits inside the words for let go of everything

parts.note: to let go of staff is to fire them
everything is all
the W of WPC, woman police constable, a British police rank; the PC left over points at the computer being protected

explanation.surface: Sacking every officer, a female police constable among them, as her own protection.
explanation.walkthrough: WPC (woman police constable, a British police rank) splits as W plus PC: the W goes in, and PC is the personal computer the protection is for.
explanation.definitionFit: A firewall is software or hardware that shields a computer from unauthorised network access.

clue.text: Returning live president's vehicles

indicators.note: returning means the word for live is read backwards

parts.note: to live is to be
Ike was the nickname of President Eisenhower; the possessive gives Ike's

explanation.surface: A former president's vehicles coming back into service.
explanation.definitionFit: Electric bicycles are vehicles, ridden with battery assistance.

clue.text: Determined to hide kiss in explicit message

indicators.note: to hide something is to cover it, so the kiss letter is concealed within the word for determined

parts.note: determined, fixed, means set
X is a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Someone resolved to leave a kiss off an explicit message.
explanation.definitionFit: A sext is a sexually explicit text sent by phone.

clue.text: Unfortunate snag in camp grooming activity

indicators.note: unfortunate suggests things gone wrong, so the letters of snag in camp are jumbled

explanation.surface: A mishap at a campsite during someone's grooming.
explanation.definitionFit: Manscaping is the trimming or shaving of male body hair, a form of personal grooming.

clue.text: Characters covered in lava: perspiring, but they aren't exactly smoking

indicators.note: the letters wanted are covered by, lying inside, the words lava perspiring

explanation.surface: Figures smeared in lava and sweating, though strictly not smoking.
explanation.definitionFit: E-cigarette users inhale vapour rather than smoke, so strictly speaking they aren't smoking.

clue.text: Put in grinding toil with hard calculus

parts.note: to put in data is to enter it

indicators.note: grinding breaks something down, so the letters of toil are rearranged

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Slogging away at hard calculus problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Calculus' looks like maths, but here it is the medical sense: a stone in the body.
explanation.definitionFit: In medicine a calculus is a stone, and an enterolith is one formed in the intestine.

clue.text: Sharing one's thoughts with cute touch, briefly

parts.note: twee means sweetly cute, sickly so

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word for touch loses its last letter

parts.note: a touch of colour is a tinge

explanation.surface: Sharing ideas with a brief, cute touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Posting on Twitter is broadcasting your opinions to followers, a modern way of airing views.

clue.text: Believer in fake news article, Republican keeping dull routine

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so the words for article and Republican go round the word for routine

parts.note: the is the definite article
a rut is a dull routine

explanation.surface: A Republican conspiracy theorist stuck in a rut, reading a fake news article.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition runs to 'news'; 'article' then starts the wordplay rather than belonging to the fake news.
explanation.definitionFit: A truther rejects official accounts of events for conspiracy theories, often spread through fake news.

clue.text: Efforts of heartless foes seizing empty Reichstag

indicators.note: seizing means grabbing hold, so the rest of foes surrounds those two letters
heartless means the middle letter of the word for foes is removed

parts.note: foes are enemies

indicators.note: empty means the inside of Reichstag is cleared out, leaving its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Enemies storming a deserted German parliament building.
explanation.walkthrough: The Reichstag is the German parliament building in Berlin.
explanation.definitionFit: Efforts and energies both mean exertions, as in putting your energies into something.

clue.text: Mass of waste paper cut by a composer

indicators.note: cut by means split open, so the letter a goes inside the paper's initials

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times newspaper
Alban Berg was an Austrian composer

explanation.surface: Waste paper shredded by a composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waste paper' seems a phrase, but 'waste' finishes the definition and 'paper' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A fatberg is a congealed lump of fat and wet wipes clogging a sewer.

clue.text: Descartes's logical bit of algebra is on news

indicators.note: a bit of these words is the stretch wanted, sitting inside algebra is on news

explanation.surface: A French philosopher's logical reasoning appears in algebra and the news.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Descartes's' signals a French word: the French for logical or reasoned.
explanation.definitionFit: The French adjective means reasoned or systematic, as in catalogue raisonné; Descartes was a French thinker.

clue.text: Shot as a dart from Caesar heavenwards

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or thrown about, so the letters of as a dart are reordered

explanation.surface: An arrow fired like a dart up into the heavens from Caesar's hand.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means 'to the stars', fitting the language Caesar spoke and the upward direction.

clue.text: Refuse further contact with a foreign fellow in red pants

parts.note: un is a in French

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters of in red are scrambled

explanation.surface: Cutting off a foreign man wearing red trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' reads as trousers; in British slang it means rubbish, hence a scramble signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To unfriend someone on social media is to remove them as a contact, ending further dealings.

clue.text: Required for reporter, any editors

indicators.note: for a reporter means as it is spoken out loud, so the word any is heard as letters

parts.note: the word any, said aloud, sounds like the two letters N and E
ED is the abbreviation for editor; two of them for editors

explanation.surface: Something a reporter needs: any editors at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Needed and required both mean necessary, wanted as essential.

clue.text: Nationalist policy from monarch getting in scrap

indicators.note: getting in means entering, so the monarch's word goes inside the word for scrap

parts.note: a scrap is a bit
rex is Latin for king, as on coins

explanation.surface: A nationalist programme from a king who gets into a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' looks like a fight but means a small piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's departure from the EU was driven by a nationalist, sovereignty-first political agenda.

clue.text: Sailors thus about to enter Rolls

indicators.note: to enter means going in, so the reversed word goes inside the word for rolls

parts.note: buns are bread rolls

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the word for thus is read backwards

parts.note: thus means so

explanation.surface: Sailors heading into a Rolls-Royce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolls' looks like the car, but it is bread rolls.
explanation.definitionFit: Bosuns, boatswains, are ship's officers in charge of rigging and deck crew: seamen.

clue.text: One new chronicle with current text, like the across answers here

indicators.note: new means remade, so the letters of one are rearranged

parts.note: a chronicle is a record or log
I is the symbol for electric current
SMS is a text message

explanation.surface: A recipe: a new chronicle with up-to-date text.
explanation.walkthrough: The across answers (VLOG, SEXT, MANSCAPING, FIREWALL, BREXIT and others) are all recently coined words.
explanation.definitionFit: Neologisms are newly coined words, which describes recent coinages filling the across lights.

clue.text: Very extensive, nameless posts online

indicators.note: nameless means without N, the abbreviation for name

parts.note: extensive means long

explanation.surface: Extremely long anonymous internet posts.
explanation.definitionFit: A vlog is a video blog, its entries posted on the web.

clue.text: Mark an X in 18 consecutive letters brought up

indicators.note: brought up in a down clue means read from bottom to top, reversing the letters

parts.note: E to V spans eighteen letters of the alphabet in order

explanation.surface: Putting a cross in a box after a run of letters is brought up.
explanation.walkthrough: '18' looks like a cross-reference to 18 down, but it counts letters: E, F, G and so on to V make eighteen, so the phrase is 'E to V'.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ballot paper you cast your choice by putting a cross in the box.

clue.text: Man United star that is as Aeneas to Achates

parts.note: George Best was a Manchester United footballing star
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: A footballer compared to a hero of Virgil's epic.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Aeneid, Achates is Aeneas's loyal companion, 'fidus Achates'; so Aeneas is his closest friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for best friend, which is what Aeneas was to his faithful companion Achates.

clue.text: Musical cycle has style and contemporary sound

parts.note: Wagner's Ring is a cycle of four operas
tone means style or manner

explanation.surface: A song cycle that has style and a modern sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A mobile phone's call alert is a modern noise that didn't exist a few decades ago.
